sections.title: Committee Objectives
sections.content: After data management discussions at a Network Working Group meeting, participants formed the Network Data Management Committee, chaired by Doug McKay of IBM. Its aims were to classify the issues and possible approaches, integrate independent activities on data sharing, and coordinate experiments to test services and compare approaches.
sections.plainLanguage: The committee was set up to organize work on network data sharing. It would identify problems, connect separate projects and coordinate experiments.

sections.title: Meeting Topics
sections.content:
An informal meeting on May 19 established an approach for the committee. The announcement called for a data management meeting at CCA in Cambridge, using a format in which organizations submitted working papers and made oral presentations.

Suggested topics included data sharing, data description and access languages, integration of data services, experiments, network data directories, and operational or control protocols. CCA planned to discuss data-computer facilities rather than the language itself.
sections.plainLanguage: Participants were asked to bring papers on data sharing, data languages, experiments, directories and control. Their discussion would help shape later work.

sections.title: Schedule and Participation
sections.content:
Position papers were requested by July 16, with receipt no later than July 19. The agenda, papers and background bibliography were to be distributed by July 23. The meeting was scheduled for August 2-4 at CCA in Cambridge.

The announcement invited people to send suggestions and asked participants to arrange lodging through CCA.
sections.plainLanguage: The committee set dates for papers and for the meeting. Participants were asked to share their work in advance and arrange their own lodging.
